subject: Fencepost rebaseline and risk ledger for MAP — Horizon Health
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@horizonhealth.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fencepost rebaseline and risk ledger for MAP — Horizon Health

Jordan / Priya —

Quick note after this morning's cadence: procurement flagged an evidence gap (SOC2 artifact request) that will push the acceptance window. Based on the current MAP activities and the outstanding items we have two sailing lanes: (A) keep the original close date and compress the acceptance canary (risk: higher ops overhead + potential quality regressions) or (B) rebaseline the close window by three weeks to allow procurement + infra canary and a controlled rollout.

I attached an updated MAP (Horizon_MAP_v3.xlsx) and a short risk ledger (Close_Risk_Ledger_20260615.csv) that enumerates the outstanding artifacts, owners, and recovery options. Highlights:
- Procurement needs SOC2 evidence (controls matrix + last audit extraction) — owner: Horizon procurement / CC: Priya
- Cloud region quotas may require a short dedicated pool for the canary — owner: Redwood infra (Marcus)
- Acceptance test windows: we can stage a 25% traffic canary for two weeks, then expand if metrics hold

Ask: can you confirm whether Horizon is comfortable with a +3 week rebaseline? If not, please indicate acceptance of the compressed canary and we will surface cost/credit implications.

If you prefer, we can run a 1:1 with procurement and legal today.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Strategic Account Manager | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Horizon_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet); Close_Risk_Ledger_20260615.csv (csv)

From: Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@horizonhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@horizonhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fencepost rebaseline and risk ledger for MAP — Horizon Health

Irene —

Thanks for the summary and the docs. Procurement is concerned about the implications of a 3-week shift on our internal program timeline. Two quick questions:
1) If we go +3 weeks, what is the proposed SLA/cost delta for the canary? We will need that spelled out before legal will touch an amendment.
2) What rollback criteria would Redwood use during the canary (latency/accuracy thresholds)?

If we can get a short matrix covering the cost delta + rollback thresholds, procurement can evaluate later today. Otherwise — our fallback is to try the compressed canary (2-week window) but that will require a firm cutover plan.

Jordan
Jordan Myers
Dir. of Digital Programs, Horizon Health
jordan.myers@horizonhealth.com | +1 617-555-9876

Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fencepost rebaseline and risk ledger for MAP — Horizon Health

Jordan / Priya —

Quick operational options from our side (short bullets so procurement can act):

Option A — +3 week rebaseline (recommended)
- Stand up a small dedicated pool for the canary (2 x A100 equiv) for 2 weeks
- Canary policy: 25% traffic, automated latency/QA rollback if 99th pctl latency > 450ms or token-level error rate increases by >1.5x over baseline
- Cost delta: estimated +$12k for the 2-week dedicated pool; Redwood prepared to offer a one-off 10% usage credit to soften the hit

Option B — Compressed canary (no rebaseline)
- Use shared pool with priority routing; 25% traffic for 1 week
- Increased risk of transient errors and slower rollbacks; ops overhead +2x
- Cost delta: nominal, but potential remediation engineering time billed separately

Attachments: Close_Risk_Ledger_20260615.csv; SOC2_evidence.pdf (we included the standard controls extract for procurement review)

If procurement is comfortable, we can prepare a short amendment (DocuSign) that encodes the dedicated pool and the 10% credit. I can also draft explicit rollback criteria and a compact runbook for acceptance.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fencepost rebaseline and risk ledger for MAP — Horizon Health

Marcus / Irene —

Procurement is provisionally ok with Option A (the +3 week rebaseline) provided we get two things in writing: (1) a cost cap (total additional spend for the canary not to exceed $15k) and (2) explicit rollback criteria and SLA that commit Redwood to revert traffic or pause expansion if metrics breach.

If Redwood can produce an amendment that includes the cost cap + the rollback thresholds you mentioned we will run it through legal this AM. We prefer DocuSign for a fast turnaround.

Priya Rao
Sr. Manager, Procurement | Horizon Health
priya.rao@horizonhealth.com | +1 617-555-3344

Subject: Escalation: SLA exception request for Horizon — need rapid approvals

Team —

Procurement (Horizon) approved the +3 week rebaseline contingent on a hard cost cap ($15k) and explicit rollback triggers. They want a DocuSign amendment today. This is time-sensitive — legal and finance need to turn in a short form amendment and we need cloud ops to be on standby to spin up the dedicated pool.

Please action:
- Laura: prepare the amendment (one paragraph + appendix with rollback criteria). Use DEAL-7481-HZ in the header and include the 10% one-off credit language.
- Camila: notify cloud ops and confirm we can provision the 2 x A100 equiv pool in us-west-2 within 6 hours of sign-off. Provide the uptime SLA we will commit for the canary window.
- Marcus: finalize the rollback thresholds and the quick-runbook (I referenced them in your note). Drop them into the HubSpot deal and link to the DocuSign draft.

I will loop legal directly if any roadblocks — Jordan / Priya are waiting. If we can get this signed by EOD Pacific we keep the MAP intact.

Irene
Irene Choi
